newsitem.title: USA: Ultramar Q3 hurt by Quebec margins.
newsitem.headline: Ultramar Q3 hurt by Quebec margins.

text.p: Ultramar Corp Wednesday reported that third quarter earnings dropped to $0.01 per share from $0.52 a year earlier citing lower industry refining and marketing margins in eastern Canada.
Chief executive Jean Gaulin "Margins were squeezed as crude prices reached a five-year high during the quarter due to supply concerns and the unrest in the Middle East.
"Our third quarter margin at the Quebec refinery was over $2 per barrel below this year's second quarter level and this reduced our pre-tax earnings approximately $25 million for the quarter.

"Although California refining margins were lower in the third quarter than in the second quarter of 1996, we had improved results from our California operation as we were able to offset the impact of the lower refining margins through improved refinery operations and higher retail marketing margins."

In California, the Wilmington refinery had an average throughput of 109,200 barrels per day in the quarter compared to 112,200 in this year's second quarter. The refining margin, at $5.21 per barrel, was over $1.00 lower than in the second quarter of this year.

Retail marketing margins in California for the company's network of 360 stations averaged $0.143 per gallon in the quarter compared to $0.109 per gallon in the second quarter of 1996. Retail marketing volumes were consistent with the second quarter of 1996 at 37,800 barrels daily.

The refining margin at the company's Quebec refinery averaged $1.53 per barrel for the quarter compared to $3.65 in the second quarter of 1996. The refinery's throughput during the quarter averaged 126,800 barrels per day compared to 147,400 in this year's second quarter.

Ultramar said throughput during the quarter was reduced due to a planned maintenance turnaround of the refinery's crude and platformer units. As a result of the very low refining margins in the third quarter, the company extended the turnaround to 17 from 10 days to do work originally planned for the Spring of 1997.

During the turnaround, the distillate hydrotreater was debottlenecked and other equipment was upgraded in order to process additional acidic crude and make 100 percent low- sulfur on-road diesel fuel. The refinery can now run an additional 25,000 barrels per day of acidic crude oil.

Retail marketing margins, which include the motorist, cardlock and home-heat businesses, averaged $0.174 per gallon in the quarter compared to $0.252 in the second quarter. It said the decline was due to the lack of heating oil sales, which carry a higher margin than the other two channels of retail trade, and strong competition in the motorist business.
Ultramar said retail marketing volumes averaged 59,600 barrels daily in the quarter compared to 54,000 in the previous quarter.

Gaulin said "refining margins on the East Coast have recovered somewhat from the extremely low levels of the third quarter. Distillate product prices have risen in response to the higher crude costs and low heating oil inventory levels and retail margins have returned to historical levels.
"However, on the West Coast, refining margins have declined early in the fourth quarter as product prices have not yet responded to the recent run-up in crude oil prices."
